# attestation-token-endpoint

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from servlets/pf-integration/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/attestation-token-endpoint.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `attestation-token-endpoint` component of `servlets/pf-integration`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.servlet.clientregistration`: generated from its catalogue, attestation-token-endpoint.json, by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Families: `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_`, `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_`, `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REFRESH_BINDING_`. A name under one of these that no catalogue declares is an unknown key.

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `ATTESTATION_AUTH` (components).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REQUIRE_HOSTED_AGENT` (system property `oidf.attestation.require_hosted_agent`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REQUIRE_HOSTED_AGENT`) | `false` | Whether an attested agent this authority does not host is refused (401); a hosted agent must be active and inside its notAfter whatever this says | **Not checked**: Anything but true, in any case, means false | Any | Yes |
| `oidf.mock.attesters` (system property) | Unset; a file path | A JWKS file of attester keys trusted directly, with no federation trust chain: a development and demo hook. The image no longer sets it from a file in the build context; a development deployment mounts the file and sets the property itself | **Not checked**: A file that cannot be read is ignored; one that can is trusted, with a warning | Not in production: any value | Yes |
| `oidf.attestation.required.claims` (system property `oidf.attestation.required.claims`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REQUIRED_CLAIMS`) | Unset; a list | The top-level claims every client attestation must carry, comma-separated, at the token-endpoint filter and the OGNL criterion alike (until 0.6.0 only the criterion read it); a client's attestation_required_claims adds to them. workload must be a non-empty object, authorization_details a non-empty array and agent_id a non-blank string; any other name must be present with a value other than null (until 0.8.0 any other name passed unchecked). The filter logs each name and its check at start. The image set workload until 0.6.0; set OIDF_ATTESTATION_REQUIRED_CLAIMS=workload to keep that | **Per request**: A name no attestation carries, a misspelling included, refuses every such request with insufficient_disclosure; check the start-up log line that lists each name | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_ACCEPTED_TYPS` (system property `oidf.attestation.accepted.typs`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_ACCEPTED_TYPS`) | `oauth-client-attestation+jwt`; a list | The client attestation typ values the token-endpoint filter accepts, comma-separated, compared without case and with an optional application/ prefix. draft-ietf-oauth-attestation-based-client-auth-11 §4 names oauth-client-attestation+jwt unless a profile (§13) names another; list a profile's typ here, and keep the draft's while clients still send it. A client's attestation_accepted_typs can only narrow this list. The PoP typ is fixed | **Per request**: An attestation whose typ is not listed is refused with invalid_client_attestation; a list of nothing stops the filter starting | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_MIN_KEY_STORAGE` (env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_MIN_KEY_STORAGE`, then system property `oidf.attestation.min.key_storage`) | Unset; one of `iso_18045_basic`, `iso_18045_enhanced-basic`, `iso_18045_moderate`, `iso_18045_high` | The lowest key_storage level every client's attestation must assert (OpenID4VCI 1.0 Appendix D.2), compared on ISO/IEC 18045 attack potential: basic < enhanced-basic < moderate < high. Unset, the default, sets no minimum. An attestation below it, without the claim, or asserting a value outside the four is refused invalid_client_attestation (401) at the token-endpoint filter and the OGNL criterion alike. A client's attestation_min_key_storage can only raise it (plan item X-E08, F-0760) | **Doesn't start**: Not one of the four levels, spelt exactly: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_MIN_USER_AUTHENTICATION` (env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_MIN_USER_AUTHENTICATION`, then system property `oidf.attestation.min.user_authentication`) | Unset; one of `iso_18045_basic`, `iso_18045_enhanced-basic`, `iso_18045_moderate`, `iso_18045_high` | The lowest user_authentication level every client's attestation must assert (OpenID4VCI 1.0 Appendix D.2), compared on ISO/IEC 18045 attack potential: basic < enhanced-basic < moderate < high. Unset, the default, sets no minimum. An attestation below it, without the claim, or asserting a value outside the four is refused invalid_client_attestation (401) at the token-endpoint filter and the OGNL criterion alike. A client's attestation_min_user_authentication can only raise it (plan item X-E08, F-0760) | **Doesn't start**: Not one of the four levels, spelt exactly: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_SINGLE_USE` (env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_SINGLE_USE`, then system property `oidf.attestation.single_use`) | `false` | Whether every client's attestation authenticates once only, at the token-endpoint filter and the OGNL criterion alike: the verifier records the attestation's SHA-256 in the replay store once its proof verifies and refuses a second presentation with use_fresh_attestation (401). A client's attestation_single_use can turn it on for that client alone. Each token then costs an issuance call to the attester, which OIDF_ATTESTER_ISSUANCE_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE (60 by default) limits per caller (F-0060): raise it to cover the token rate of every single-use client (plan item X-E06, F-0750) | **Doesn't start**: Not true or false: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REQUIRED_TRUST_MARKS` (env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REQUIRED_TRUST_MARKS`, then system property `oidf.attestation.required.trust_marks`) | Unset; a list | The OpenID Federation Trust Mark types every client's attester must hold, space- or comma-separated, at the token-endpoint filter and the OGNL criterion alike (plan item X-E07, F-0755). Once the attester's trust chain validates, it is refused invalid_client_attestation (401) unless its Entity Configuration carries a valid mark of each type: issued by an issuer the Trust Anchor's trust_mark_issuers recognises for the type, signed, about the attester and unexpired (OpenID Federation 1.0 §7, §7.3). A verdict that lets an attester through is reused until the earliest of the marks' exp, the chain's expiry and OIDF_ATTESTATION_TRUST_MARK_CACHE_MAX_SECONDS. An attester trusted through oidf.mock.attesters holds no marks, so any requirement refuses it (fail closed). A client's attestation_required_trust_marks adds to this list for that client and can never remove a type from it. Unset checks no marks | **Per request**: A type no attester's marks carry, a misspelling included, refuses every attestation with invalid_client_attestation and attestation.attester.trust_marks_refused; a list of nothing stops the filter starting | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_TRUST_MARK_CACHE_MAX_SECONDS` (env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_TRUST_MARK_CACHE_MAX_SECONDS`, then system property `oidf.attestation.trust_mark_cache_max_seconds`) | `3600`; a whole number, 0 to 86400 | The longest a node reuses a verdict that let a client attester through on the Trust Marks its client's policy requires, in seconds (plan item X-E07). The verdict lapses sooner at the earliest exp among the marks it rested on or at the trust chain's expiry. A reused verdict asks no Trust Mark status endpoint, so with OIDF_FEDERATION_TRUST_MARK_STATUS_CHECK on this bounds how long a mark revoked at its issuer stays accepted; with it off (the default) no status endpoint is asked and a revoked mark is accepted until its own exp. 0 decides every request afresh; a refusal is never reused | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 0 to 86400: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REDECIDE_ON_REFRESH_TYPES` | `payment_initiation,account_information`; a list | The authorization_details types, comma-separated, whose refresh must repeat its authorization_details: the issued-details criterion (IssuedDetailsCriterion.withinCeiling on an access-token mapping) refuses a refresh that sends none for a grant holding a detail of one of them, so the client asks again with its details and PingFederate calls the RAR processor's enrich, and so the PDP, again. PingFederate reissues a bare refresh's stored details without asking (F-0105). Only mappings that carry the criterion apply it; blank sends no refresh back | **Not checked**: Read as given; a type no grant holds sends nothing back | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REFRESH_BINDING` (system property `oidf.attestation.refresh_binding`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REFRESH_BINDING`) | `on`; one of `off`, `on`, `strict` | Whether the token-endpoint filter binds a refresh token to the client instance key it was issued under (ABCA-11 §10.3, plan item X-E15). on, the default: a refresh token issued to a request authenticated by an attestation is recorded against the SHA-256 of the token and the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the attestation's cnf key, in the attestation store (Redis when OIDF_REDIS_URL is set); a refresh with that token is refused 400 invalid_grant unless it is authenticated by an attestation whose cnf key is that key, and the rotated token is bound in its place. A refresh token with no binding recorded (issued before 0.8.0, or by a client that did not authenticate with an attestation) is let through with the event attestation.refresh.unbound and counted. strict refuses that too, 400 invalid_grant. off records and checks nothing. A store that cannot be read or written is 503 temporarily_unavailable, and an issued token whose binding cannot be recorded is withheld and its grant revoked. A client's attestation_refresh_binding can only tighten this | **Doesn't start**: Not off, on or strict: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting. off under the production profile without refresh-binding-off in OIDF_ACCEPTED_RISKS: ATTESTATION_AUTH is refused, naming the risk | In production only as accepted risk `refresh-binding-off`: `off`; refuses `ATTESTATION_AUTH` | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REFRESH_BINDING_TTL_SECONDS` (system property `oidf.attestation.refresh_binding.ttl_seconds`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REFRESH_BINDING_TTL_SECONDS`) | `31536000`; a whole number, 3600 to 315360000 | How long a refresh token's binding is kept when PingFederate does not say when the token expires, in seconds (plan item X-E15). Each binding is kept until its grant's expiry as PingFederate's AccessGrantManager reports it; a grant with no expiry, or one that cannot be read, is kept this long, 365 days by default. Set it at least as long as the longest refresh-token lifetime you issue: a binding that expires before its token makes the token unknown, let through under on and refused under strict | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 3600 to 315360000: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REFRESH_BINDING_GRACE_SECONDS` (system property `oidf.attestation.refresh_binding.grace_seconds`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_REFRESH_BINDING_GRACE_SECONDS`) | Unset; a whole number, 0 to 2592000 | How long a refresh token replaced by rotation stays bound to its instance key, in seconds (plan item X-E15, F-0790). PingFederate's refresh-token rolling grace period keeps the old token redeemable for a while, and a token with no binding is let through under on with any key, so the old binding is never simply dropped. Unset, the default and the safe choice, keeps it until it lapses with its grant. A value shortens it to that many seconds after the rotation: set it no shorter than the longest rolling grace period in PingFederate, the server's or any client's. 0 drops it at rotation, only for a PingFederate with no grace period anywhere | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 0 to 2592000: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting. Shorter than a PingFederate grace period: the old token, once its binding is gone, is let through under on with any instance key for the rest of the grace period | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_MODE` (system property `oidf.client.revocation.mode`, then env `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_MODE`) | Unset; one of `off`, `live`, `status_list`, `both` | How the token-endpoint filter checks, at every attested authentication, that the client instance an attestation names may still authenticate (plan items X-E11, X-E12): live reads the instance and agent registers and refuses an attestation whose agent_id a register holds suspended or revoked; status_list reads the attestation's status claim (draft-ietf-oauth-status-list-21 section 6.2) from the attester's Token Status List, fetched and cached under OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_* and verified with the attester's keys, and refuses an entry that is not VALID (INVALID, SUSPENDED, another value or an index outside the list) and an attestation without the claim; both does both. A refusal is 401 invalid_client (the attestation is valid, the client's standing is not) at the token, PAR, CIBA, device authorization and introspection endpoints, refresh included, though the attestation is unexpired; the revocation endpoint is left open so a revoked agent can still revoke its own tokens. Under live, an agent_id no register knows, and an attestation without one, pass unless the client's attestation_revocation_mode is live. Unset is live when either register is configured (OIDF_AGENT_REGISTRY_MODE not off, or OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_DATA_STORE_ID set), otherwise off. The OGNL issuance criterion runs the same checks for a request the filter did not verify, in a deployment without the filter; it runs in PingFederate's engine copy, which cannot read the registers, so there a live check that applies refuses every attested token (set off or status_list to keep such a deployment issuing); the status list it can fetch | **Doesn't start**: Not off, live, status_list or both: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting. off under the production profile without client-revocation-off in OIDF_ACCEPTED_RISKS: ATTESTATION_AUTH is refused, naming the risk. live or both with no register configured: the filter does not start under production, naming the setting; under development a WARN, and it checks only clients whose attestation_revocation_mode is live, which are then refused. status_list or both with attesters that mint no status claim: every attestation is refused 401 invalid_client. A list that cannot be fetched or verified: the request is refused 503 temporarily_unavailable (development's OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_FAIL_OPEN lets it on). live (or unset) over a register in a deployment without the token-endpoint filter: nothing refuses it at start-up, which cannot see such a deployment; the issuance criterion, which cannot read the registers, refuses every attested token the check applies to, active clients included, and its first call logs one line naming the setting and the filter, ERROR under production and WARN under development. Set off or status_list, or install the filter | In production only as accepted risk `client-revocation-off`: `off`; refuses `ATTESTATION_AUTH` | Yes |
| `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_CACHE_SECONDS` (system property `oidf.client.revocation.cache_seconds`, then env `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_CACHE_SECONDS`) | `0`; a whole number, 0 to 300 | How long a node remembers that an instance is active, in seconds (plan item X-E11). 0, the default, reads the register at every attested authentication, so a suspension or revocation takes effect at the next request. Above 0 saves the read at the price of a revocation that many seconds late on every other node (the node that takes a suspension or revocation in this webapp forgets that agent at once, F-0773); only an active answer is remembered, never a refusal or an unreachable register | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 0 to 300: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_FAIL_OPEN` (system property `oidf.client.revocation.fail_open`, then env `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_FAIL_OPEN`) | `false` | Development only: whether an attested request goes on, with a WARN, when the instance or agent register cannot be read or has not started, or the attestation's Token Status List cannot be fetched or verified (X-E12). Off, the default and the only value production takes, refuses it 503 temporarily_unavailable (owner decision, 2026-10-15) | **Doesn't start**: Not true or false: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting. true under the production profile: listed as a violation in the start-up audit, which refuses no component (the setting names none); the filter starts and ignores it, so an unreadable register is still refused 503 | Not in production: `true` | Yes |
| `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_DATA_STORE_ID` (system property `oidf.instance.registry.data_store_id`, then env `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_DATA_STORE_ID`) | Unset | A PingFederate JDBC data store on the Identity Object Model's PostgreSQL, whose pool PingFederate reads device instances through (plan item X-E11): the token endpoint's revocation check and the operator API at /federation/attestation/instances/*. The database must carry the model's agent-instance migrations (idm.schema_migration). Unset, PingFederate reads no device instances | **Per request**: An unknown id, an unreachable database or a model schema behind: InstanceRegistryListener's part of ATTESTATION_AUTH is FAILED_DEPENDENCY (retried) or FAILED_CONFIG, and every attested request is refused 503 until it starts | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_JDBC_URL` (system property `oidf.instance.registry.jdbc.url`, then env `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_JDBC_URL`) | Unset | A direct PostgreSQL JDBC URL for the device-instance registry, for development; wins over OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_DATA_STORE_ID. Never shown in the start-up banner | **Per request**: Set under production: ATTESTATION_AUTH is REFUSED. Unreachable: the listener's part is FAILED_DEPENDENCY and retried, and attested requests are refused 503 until it starts | Not in production: any value | Yes |
| `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_JDBC_USERNAME` (system property `oidf.instance.registry.jdbc.username`, then env `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_JDBC_USERNAME`) | Unset | The user for OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_JDBC_URL | **Per request**: Wrong: the listener's part is FAILED_DEPENDENCY and retried, and attested requests are refused 503 | Any | No |
| `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_JDBC_PASSWORD` (system property `oidf.instance.registry.jdbc.password`, then env `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_JDBC_PASSWORD`); or from the file `oidf.instance.registry.jdbc.password.file` or `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_JDBC_PASSWORD_FILE` names | Unset; a secret, never shown | The password for OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_JDBC_URL, or read from the file OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_JDBC_PASSWORD_FILE names | **Per request**: Wrong: the listener's part is FAILED_DEPENDENCY and retried, and attested requests are refused 503 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_MS` (system property `oidf.instance.registry.timeout.ms`, then env `OIDF_INSTANCE_REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_MS`) | `2000`; milliseconds, 100 to 10000 | Each device-instance registry database operation's budget, in milliseconds, from 100 to 10000 (plan item X-E11). The revocation check reads the registry on every attested token request's thread, so a slow database answers 503 temporarily_unavailable after this long rather than holding the PingFederate worker for the platform's 10-second default. 2000 by default, as the PDP connect timeout and the SPIRE reader's | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 100 to 10000: InstanceRegistryListener's part of ATTESTATION_AUTH is FAILED_CONFIG, naming the setting. Too short for the database: attested requests are refused 503 when a read takes longer | Any | No |
| `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_MAX_BYTES` (system property `oidf.client.revocation.status.max.bytes`, then env `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_MAX_BYTES`) | `1048576`; a whole number, 1024 to 16777216 | The largest Status List Token response body, in bytes, the token endpoint reads when it fetches an attestation's status list (plan item X-E12; 1 MiB by default, 1 KiB to 16 MiB); a larger body is refused unread past the limit | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 1024 to 16777216: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting. Too small for an attester's list: every attestation pointing to it is answered 503 temporarily_unavailable, counted as oidf_client_revocation_status_fetches_total{result=too_large} | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_MAX_LIST_BYTES` (system property `oidf.client.revocation.status.max.list.bytes`, then env `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_MAX_LIST_BYTES`) | `16777216`; a whole number, 1024 to 134217728 | The largest inflated Status List, in bytes, the token endpoint decompresses (plan item X-E12; 16 MiB by default, 1 KiB to 128 MiB): decompression stops once the output passes it, so a compressed bomb costs at most this much memory per fetch | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 1024 to 134217728: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting. Too small for an attester's list (this repository's attesters publish 256 KiB lists): every attestation pointing to it is answered 503 temporarily_unavailable, counted under result=invalid | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_TTL_MIN` (system property `oidf.client.revocation.status.ttl.min`, then env `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_TTL_MIN`) | `60`; seconds, 0 to 3600 | The shortest time, in seconds, the token endpoint trusts a fetched Status List Token before fetching it again, whatever smaller ttl it carries (plan item X-E12, draft-ietf-oauth-status-list-21 section 11.5); its exp still ends it sooner | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 0 to 3600, or above OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_TTL_MAX: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting. Too large: a revocation is seen up to this much later | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_TTL_MAX` (system property `oidf.client.revocation.status.ttl.max`, then env `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_TTL_MAX`) | `3600`; seconds, 60 to 86400 | The longest time, in seconds, the token endpoint trusts a fetched Status List Token before fetching it again, whatever larger ttl it carries, and the time a token with no ttl is trusted (plan item X-E12); its exp still ends it sooner. This repository's attesters publish a ttl of OIDF_ATTESTER_STATUS_LIST_TTL or ENROLMENT_STATUS_LIST_TTL, 300 seconds by default | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 60 to 86400, or below OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_TTL_MIN: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting. Too large: a revocation is seen up to this much later | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_STALE_GRACE` (system property `oidf.client.revocation.status.stale.grace`, then env `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_STALE_GRACE`) | `0`; seconds, 0 to 900 | How long, in seconds, a Status List Token past its freshness stays usable at the token endpoint while it cannot be fetched again (plan item X-E12; 0 by default, at most 900), never past its exp; after that an attestation pointing to it is answered 503 temporarily_unavailable | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 0 to 900: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting. Above 0: a revocation published while the attester's list is unreachable is seen up to this much later | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` (system property `oidf.client.revocation.status.cache.max.bytes`, then env `OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`) | `67108864`; a whole number, 1048576 to 1073741824 | The most inflated Status List bytes, in all, each node keeps in the token endpoint's cache of attesters' status lists (plan item X-E12; 64 MiB by default, 1 MiB to 1 GiB, and never below OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_MAX_LIST_BYTES); past it the least recently used lists are dropped and fetched again when next needed | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 1048576 to 1073741824, or below OIDF_CLIENT_REVOCATION_STATUS_MAX_LIST_BYTES: the token-endpoint attestation filter does not start, naming the setting. Too small for the lists in use: they are fetched again more often, each fetch counted in oidf_client_revocation_status_fetches_total | Any | Yes |
